# Fraud Detection MLOps

A production-shaped MLOps reference implementation for real-time bank-account-fraud
detection. The system trains a reproducible, signed model with an evaluation gate,
serves it from a model registry behind a FastAPI service, and instruments the full
serving and monitoring loop. The entire stack runs locally via `docker compose` with
no cloud dependency: MinIO stands in for S3, Postgres backs the MLflow registry, and
Prometheus, Grafana, and Evidently provide observability and drift detection.

The intent is to demonstrate the four MLOps pillars end to end (reproducible
training and registry hardening, hardened serving, monitoring and drift detection,
and testing and CI) on a realistic, class-imbalanced problem, while keeping the
deployment topology faithful to a cloud design that would cost nothing to run.

## Problem and dataset

The task is binary classification on the [Bank Account Fraud (BAF) dataset](https://github.com/feedzai/bank-account-fraud)
(NeurIPS 2022, Feedzai), a privacy-preserving, synthetically generated dataset derived
from a real-world bank-account-opening portfolio. The `Base` variant is 1,000,000
tabular applications with 32 columns and a fraud prevalence of approximately 1.1 percent.

Fraud detection is a cost-asymmetric, heavily imbalanced problem. Raw accuracy is
meaningless at 1 percent prevalence, and a model that maximizes recall without
constraint floods analysts with false positives. The model is therefore optimized for
**recall at a fixed false-positive-rate budget** rather than a thresholded label
metric: the operating point is chosen to hold FPR at approximately 5 percent, and the
decision threshold is selected from the ROC curve and tracked as model metadata rather
than hardcoded.

The model is trained on the earliest months of data and evaluated on the most recent
held-out months, a temporal split that mirrors production (fit on the past, score the
future) and keeps future-month rows out of training. On that holdout, performance at the
5 percent FPR operating point is approximately 0.55 recall and 0.89 ROC-AUC, the figures
the promotion gate is calibrated against (recall floor 0.45, FPR ceiling 0.06).

## Architecture

```
                       ┌──────────────┐    scrape    ┌──────────────┐
   client ───────────▶ │   FastAPI    │ ───────────▶ │  Prometheus  │ ──▶ Grafana
   (REST / static UI)  │   serving    │   /metrics   └──────────────┘    (dashboards)
                       └──────┬───────┘                      ▲
                              │ load models:/fraud_xgb@champion
                              ▼                              │ push (drift gauge)
                       ┌──────────────┐  artifacts   ┌──────────────┐
                       │    MLflow    │ ───────────▶ │  MinIO (S3)  │   ┌──────────────┐
                       │ tracking +   │  metadata    └──────────────┘   │ Pushgateway  │
                       │   registry   │ ───────────▶ ┌──────────────┐   └──────▲───────┘
                       └──────┬───────┘              │   Postgres   │          │
                              ▲                      └──────────────┘   ┌──────┴───────┐
                  train +     │                                         │  Evidently   │
                  promote     │                                         │  drift job   │
                       ┌──────┴───────┐                                 └──────────────┘
                       │   training   │  reference snapshot ───────────────────▲
                       │   pipeline   │
                       └──────────────┘
```

All services are defined in a single `docker-compose.yml`. The core stack (Postgres,
MinIO, MLflow) starts by default; serving, monitoring, and orchestration are gated
behind Compose profiles so each pillar can be brought up independently.

## Key design decisions

These are the decisions that separate this from a notebook-to-Flask prototype.

- **A single feature transform, shared by training and serving.** The preprocessing
  (sentinel imputation, one-hot encoding, passthrough) is an sklearn `ColumnTransformer`
  fitted once during training and logged as part of the model pipeline. Serving loads
  that exact fitted object, so there is no second implementation of the transform and
  no train/serve skew. This eliminates the prototype's manual `get_dummies` plus
  `expected_columns.json` realignment.

- **The model is logged with a signature and input example.** The MLflow signature
  describes the raw request the API sends, which makes train/serve contract mismatches
  a load-time error rather than a silent wrong prediction.

- **SMOTE lives inside the training pipeline, not the artifact.** Resampling is an
  `imblearn` pipeline step that fires only at `fit` and is a no-op at predict. The
  served model is rebuilt as a plain sklearn pipeline with the sampler stripped, which
  keeps `imbalanced-learn` (a training-only dependency) out of the serving image.

- **Resampling happens after the split.** SMOTE is applied only to the training fold;
  the test set retains the real ~1 percent prevalence, so reported metrics are not
  inflated by synthetic minority examples leaking into evaluation.

- **Evaluation uses a temporal split, not a random one.** The model trains on the
  earliest months and is scored on the most recent held-out months, so the metrics
  reflect predicting the future from the past and no future-month row can leak into
  training. `month` is deliberately excluded from the model's inputs. As a raw calendar
  index it carries no generalizing signal and would only invite temporal leakage; it
  serves solely as the split key and the drift axis.

- **Promotion is gated.** Training registers every run, but the `@champion` alias only
  moves if the model clears the recall and FPR gate. The decision threshold is stored
  as a model-version tag and read by the serving layer, so the operating point travels
  with the model instead of being a magic constant in the API.

- **Drift is the leading signal; the gate is the lagging one.** Data drift (label-free)
  is computed against a frozen reference snapshot and is the intended retraining
  trigger. Model performance, which depends on delayed ground-truth labels, governs
  whether a retrained candidate is allowed to ship. This mirrors how fraud labels
  actually arrive: late and biased toward investigated cases.

- **The serving layer records what it scores.** Every `/predict` request is appended to
  a rolling `current.parquet`, which the scheduled drift job compares against the frozen
  training reference. Drift is therefore measured on real received traffic (from any
  client) and is fully decoupled from how that traffic was generated.

## Repository layout

```
src/fraud_detection/
  config.py              Typed, environment-driven settings (pydantic-settings)
  features.py            Shared feature contract: prepare_X + ColumnTransformer
  data.py                Loading, pandera input schema, leakage-safe split
  evaluate.py            FPR-budget threshold selection and the promotion gate
  train.py               Reproducible pipeline: fit, gate, log signed model, register
  serving/
    app.py               FastAPI app: registry load, /predict, /health, /metrics
    schemas.py           Pydantic request/response contract
  monitoring/
    drift.py             Evidently data-drift: report, JSON summary, metric push
    traffic.py           Captures live /predict payloads to current.parquet (drift input)
monitoring/
  prometheus/            Scrape config
  grafana/               Provisioned datasource + dashboard
  evidently/run_drift.py CLI wrapper over fraud_detection.monitoring.drift
pipelines/dags/          Airflow retrain and drift DAGs (in progress)
tests/
  unit/                  Feature contract, schema rejection, gate logic, drift mapping
  integration/           API behavior against a real loaded model
infra/                   Postgres init, Terraform mirror (optional)
docker-compose.yml       Full local stack, organized by profile
Dockerfile               Serving image (serve dependencies only)
```

## Quickstart

Prerequisites: Docker with Compose, Python 3.11, and Poetry.

```bash
# 1. Configuration (local defaults are safe; never commit a real .env)
cp .env.example .env

# 2. Install the project and its dependency groups
poetry install --with train,dev

# 3. Bring up the core stack (Postgres, MinIO, MLflow)
make up
```

Service endpoints once the stack is running:

| Service      | URL                     | Profile        |
| ------------ | ----------------------- | -------------- |
| MLflow       | http://localhost:5001   | core           |
| MinIO console| http://localhost:9001   | core           |
| FastAPI      | http://localhost:8000   | serving        |
| Prometheus   | http://localhost:9090   | monitoring     |
| Grafana      | http://localhost:3000   | monitoring     |
| Pushgateway  | http://localhost:9091   | monitoring     |

Bring up additional pillars by profile, for example:

```bash
docker compose --profile serving up -d
docker compose --profile monitoring up -d
```

### Training

The training data is not committed. Download the BAF `Base.csv` from the
[dataset repository](https://github.com/feedzai/bank-account-fraud) and place it at
`notebooks/data/Base.csv` (or set `TRAIN_DATA_PATH`). Then:

```bash
make train
```

This fits the pipeline, selects the threshold at the target FPR, logs a signed model
with its metrics and threshold, writes the drift reference snapshot, and, against a
running MLflow registry, registers the model and promotes it to `@champion` if it
passes the gate.

### Serving and prediction

With the `serving` profile up and a champion promoted, the API loads
`models:/fraud_xgb@champion` at startup. A health check and a sample prediction:

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/health

curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/predict \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @- <<'JSON'
{ ...raw transaction fields per schemas.TransactionPayload... }
JSON
```

The response returns the fraud probability, the binary decision at the model's
threshold, the threshold itself, and the serving model version.

### Drift check

```bash
python monitoring/evidently/run_drift.py \
  --reference data/reference.parquet \
  --current  <recent_traffic.parquet>
```

This produces an Evidently HTML report and a JSON summary, and pushes a drift gauge to
the Pushgateway when `PROMETHEUS_PUSHGATEWAY_URL` is set. In the running stack the
`--current` file is produced automatically: the serving API appends every scored request
to `data/current.parquet`, so the scheduled drift job reads live traffic with no manual
capture step.

## Testing and CI

```bash
make test    # pytest: unit + integration
make lint    # ruff check + format check
```

Unit tests cover the feature contract, the pandera schema's rejection behavior, the
FPR-budget threshold and promotion-gate logic, and the drift column mapping.
Integration tests drive the real FastAPI app against a tiny model trained through the
production pipeline, asserting the prediction contract, input validation, and metric
exposure. GitHub Actions runs lint, the test suite, and a serving-image build on every
push and pull request.

## Notes

This is a portfolio reference implementation. It runs locally at zero cloud cost while
preserving a topology that maps cleanly onto managed cloud services (S3, a managed
Postgres, a tracking server, and a container runtime). Because the BAF dataset is
static, drift is demonstrated by controlled, deliberate distribution shifts rather than
organic change; that is called out explicitly wherever drift is exercised. A forthcoming
traffic simulator (Phase 9) replays the benchmark's own temporal and cross-variant shifts
through the live API to exercise the drift → retrain loop end to end.
